Real-time statistics are vital information for athletes and coaches, but the International Tennis Federation (ITF) could only offer high-level post-match summary data. Using Azure Databricks, Azure SQL Database, Microsoft Surface, and Azure Data Lake—ITF and Valorem Reply developed the Billie Jean King Cup Match Insights app to support teams with performance insights during matches. The app empowers tennis professionals to elevate their game, make data-driven decisions, and achieve better results on the court.

Tennis is one of the world’s oldest and most universal sports, with more than 87 million players and 1.2 billion fans across the globe. The International Tennis Federation (ITF), based in the UK, runs six major global tours and 3,000 events a year providing competitive opportunities for players of all ages. ITF flagship events include the Billie Jean King Cup, Davis Cup, and the Olympic and Paralympic tennis events.

The new application uses input from camera-based player and ball tracking systems to provide players and coaches with detailed metrics, enabling them to gain insights into player performance in near real time during matches. The application aims to improve the way tennis information is analyzed, offering in-depth statistics and visualizations for strategic decision-making. “We’ve heard from players that they find having the data to be very valuable because they can react faster—and the data verifies their own observations,” says Jamie Capel-Davies, Head of Science & Technical, ITF. “We’re excited to see how the teams are studying the analytics to adjust their match strategy in the moment.”
